articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Atila Fassina)
articles.description: We, as human beings, don’t worry too much about making sure the connections land at the right point. Our brain just works that way, declaratively. However, for building AI, we need to be more explicit. Let’s dive in!

articles.description: Design leaders are expected to deliver the impossible. Instead of trying, we need to redefine our role from implementor to enabler.

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Olivia De Alba)
articles.description: There are many ways to elevate a design project from good to incredible. For web and product designers, it’s not just about adding more animations and flair. What it truly comes down to is a reframing of your thought processes starting before the project even kicks off. Olivia De Alba presents three approaches that designers can implement and which will change the way they make their projects more successful.

I Göteborg har Västtrafik ställt in busstrafiken på vissa sträckor på grund av halka, det handlar om åtta busslinjer, bland annat röd express i Landvetter. Spårvagnstrafiken är inte påverkad.

articles.description:
• Donald Trumps valseger i november har nu officiellt fastslagits av USA:s kongress. Kongressens båda kamrar i Washington har som traditionen och USA:s grundlag föreskriver fastslagit de förseglade elektorsrösterna från respektive delstat.

  • Ceremonin i kongressbyggnaden Kapitolium leddes av Kamala Harris, eftersom vicepresidenten är ordförande i senaten. 

  • Nästa steg i maktöverförandet sker den 20 januari. Då installeras Donald Trump som USA:s 47:e president. Det är nu exakt fyra år sedan som motsvarande ceremoni avbröts efter att Trumpanhängare stormat Kapitolium.

articles.description:

  • Trudeaus finansminister avgick i december, enligt henne vill hon ha en hårdare linje mot Trump.

  • ”Det kan bli långa avstängningar. Framförallt många bilar som fastnar och då blir det dominoeffekt”, säger Kim Hellberg, trafikreporter på Sveriges Radio.

  • Beskedet kommer efter en tid med minskad popularitet och efter att avgångskrav väckts inom partiet. 

  • Justin Trudeau har varit premiärminister sedan 2015 och partiledare sedan 2013.
articles.title: Kanadas premiärminister Justin Trudeau kommer avgå

articles.description:

  • Musk är kritisk till att regeringen sagt nej till en utredning om den skandal som uppdagades i Oldham för drygt tio år sedan när unga flickor utsattes för sexuella övergrepp av män, där många hade bakgrund i Pakistan.

  • Starmer riktade också hård kritik mot det konservativa Torypartiet, som nu vill ha en ny utredning, men som under sina år vid makten inte genomförde de åtgärder en tidigare utredning föreslagit.

  • Kickl kommer nu sannolikt att förhandla med just ÖVP och kan bli den första förbundskanslern i Österrike från FPÖ.

  • ”Det har kommit rätt så mycket i natt, tio centimeter eller någonting”, säger snöröjaren Lukas Fohlin. Och färdtjänstchauffören Amin El Mrani konstaterar att ”det är inte så lätt”.

  • I Kansas har is och snö lagt sig över hela delstaten och i Indiana har nationalgardet kallats in för att hjälpa bilister som fastnat i snödrivor eller kört av vägarna.

  • Vädermyndigheten National weather service, NWS, säger att det är de värsta vinterstormarna på ett årtionde för de berörda områdena.

  • Under morgonen och förmiddagen påverkas framför allt de södra och västra delarna av Sverige.

  • Enligt Trafikverket är det lugnt på vägarna och det finns beredskap med tungbärgare längs de stora vägarna för att kunna dra loss lastbilar som kan köra fast.

articles.description: On 8 January 2025, the ESA/JAXA BepiColombo mission will fly just 295 km above Mercury's surface, with a closest approach scheduled for 06:59 CET (05:59 UTC). It will use this opportunity to photograph Mercury, make unique measurements of the planet’s environment, and fine-tune science instrument operations before the main mission begins. This sixth and final flyby will reduce the spacecraft’s speed and change its direction, readying it for entering orbit around the tiny planet in late 2026.
articles.title: BepiColombo to swing by Mercury for the sixth time

The accompanying audio is a sonification based on the detected flares and the spacecraft's distance to the Sun.

An ethereal dance of misty clouds of interstellar dust with a myriad of distant stars and galaxies speckled like paint drops over a black canvas. This is a sonification of a breathtaking image taken by ESA's Euclid space telescope of the young star-forming region Messier 78.

articles.description: Our understanding of planet formation in the Universe’s early days is challenged by new data from the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope. Webb solved a puzzle by proving a controversial finding made with the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope more than 20 years ago.
articles.title: Planet-forming discs lived longer in early Universe

articles.description:
Video: 
			00:01:22
				
On 9 December 2024, the Smile Platform arrived safely at Amsterdam Schiphol airport and was subsequently transported to ESA's European Space Research and Technology Centre (ESTEC) in Noordwijk, the Netherlands. It came a long way, having travelled all the way from Shanghai, China.  
This marks an important step in the Smile mission, as the spacecraft's two halves are now in the same location, ready to be joined together. Launching in around a year from now, Smile will study space weather and the interaction between the solar wind and Earth’s environment. 
The Platform, built by the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), includes the propulsion and service modules responsible for powering, steering and controlling the spacecraft. The European half of the spacecraft –  the so-called Payload Module – was built by Airbus in Madrid and is already at ESTEC. It hosts three of the four science instruments of the mission, commands all four of them and downlinks all the data back to Earth. 
The Platform didn't travel alone. It was accompanied by a team of Smile engineers and managers from CAS. They will closely work together with their European counterparts from ESA and Airbus during the coming ten months to assemble the Smile spacecraft and fully test it at ESA's ESTEC Test Centre. 
After that, Smile will be shipped to Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana. Its launch is planned for late 2025. 
All Let's Smile videos will be listed here: Let's Smile
articles.title: Smile's other half arrives | Let’s Smile (action snippet)

articles.description: For the first time, the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope has detected and ‘weighed’ a galaxy, in the early Universe, that has a mass that is similar to what our Milky Way galaxy’s mass might have been at the same stage of development. Found at around 600 million years after the Big Bang, this lightweight galaxy, nicknamed the Firefly Sparkle, is gleaming with star clusters – 10 in total – that researchers examined in great detail. Other galaxies Webb has detected at this period in the history of the Universe are significantly more massive.
articles.title: Webb finds primeval star-forming galaxy that is lightweight

articles.description: Today, ESA’s powerful X-ray observatory, XMM-Newton, celebrates 25 years in space. From planets to black holes, the space telescope has delivered many ground-breaking observations of a variety of celestial objects. And the mission is still going strong as recent results testify. We take a look at five fascinating discoveries from the last five years.
articles.title: XMM-Newton celebrates 25 years of breakthroughs

articles.description: On 1 December 2024, BepiColombo flew past Mercury for the fifth time. During this flyby, BepiColombo became the first spacecraft ever to observe Mercury in mid-infrared light. The new images reveal variations in temperature and composition across the planet's cratered surface.
articles.title: BepiColombo reveals Mercury in a new light

Over some number of pages, that fog is pushed back and the world in the book begins to populate the formerly-empty space. Eventually, that space is on the other side of a portal that I step through as effortlessly as I open the cover of the book.
